title: Little boy dancing to DJ on Boston Common has hundreds of thousands of new fans
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Four-year-old Chukwuemeka Ikesinachi-Nwogwugwu gained attention after a video of him dancing on Boston Common went viral.
The video, shared by his mother Chidimma Ikesinachi, received over 200,000 likes and 4,000 comments on social media.
Local DJ Miss S. Peace held the event to promote human connection, where Chukwuemeka was encouraged to dance by attendee Kelly Werme.

title: Boston wine bar will keep its signature pours, just without the wine
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Barcelona Wine Bar will use juice and soda for porrón pours after liquor license suspension.
The suspension followed incidents of serving alcohol to seven underage patrons in May.
The restaurant updated its ID policy and purchased more scanners after the violations.

title: Could Mike Vrabel keep 7 wide receivers on Patriots’ roster?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Mike Vrabel considers maintaining seven wide receivers on the Patriots' 53-man roster for the upcoming season.
A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism are the seven wideouts.
Trade rumors surround Kayshon Boutte despite his strong performance, while Kyle Williams aims to solidify his role in training camp.

title: Suffolk DA candidates dispute ethics, transparency, experience at Roxbury debate
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Suffolk DA candidates debated ethics and transparency, focusing on past controversies and police accountability policies.
Kevin Hayden, Rachael Rollins, and Linda Champion presented differing visions on transparency of police misconduct investigations.
Candidates discussed experience, with Hayden emphasizing his term and Rollins her broader legal experience, while Champion highlighted community work.

title: What Boston meteorologists are saying about this weekend’s humidity levels, the potential for pop-up storms
author: Heather Alterisio
bullets: Heat Advisory in effect for southern New England with temperatures feeling close to 100°F this afternoon.
Humidity remains high throughout the weekend with potential pop-up showers and storms on Friday and Saturday evenings.
Sunday expected to remain dry, but humid conditions will persist with dew points in the 60s.

title: Here’s some background behind the vintage baseball glove a Red Sox fan gave to Aroldis Chapman
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman received a vintage 1930s Bob Feller model glove from fan Andy Zides.
Chapman surrendered a two-run home run after receiving the glove, ending his streak of no earned runs.
The Red Sox defeated the White Sox 12-11 in 13 innings at Fenway Park on Thursday.

title: K-pop superstars BTS prepped for their Gillette shows at Planet Fitness in Downtown Crossing, apparently
author: Peter Chianca
bullets: BTS members Jung Hoseok, Kim Taehyung, and Jung Kook worked out at Planet Fitness in Downtown Crossing this week.
Jaeyon Jung-kook shared their Planet Fitness visit on Instagram, highlighting their courteous behavior by wiping down equipment.
BTS outperformed Taylor Swift this year, headlining sold-out shows at Gillette Stadium, according to Forbes Korea.

title: Meet Marty: Cape Cod’s newest great white shark is sticking around
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Marty, a 10-foot great white shark, is the first identified by the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy in 2026.
The shark, named after Stop & Shop's robot, has been detected 15 times off North Truro since July 16.
Stop & Shop sells plush toys of Marty, donating 20% of proceeds to the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy.

title: 5 restaurants we can’t wait to try in August
author: Jillian Dara
bullets: About Thyme, a Lebanese bakery in Harvard Square, opens in early August offering wraps, labneh, and coffee drinks.
Nana's Green Tea opens on Newbury Street with a focus on matcha-inspired drinks and Japanese parfaits.
Salt & Straw opens in Seaport with Boston-themed ice cream flavors like Boston Cream Pie and Pistachio Cannoli.

title: Boston University joins growing list of colleges expanding financial aid
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boston University will cap annual attendance costs at $20,000 for students from families earning under $200,000 starting 2026-27.
Families earning $75,000 or less will pay no cost, with financial aid covering full tuition and part of housing expenses.
This initiative follows a trend in expanding financial aid options among colleges like MIT, Harvard, and Tufts for middle-income families.
